answer: The strongest sybil defense is slow trust: influence equals account age times honest epochs, so a fresh identity starts near zero and cannot buy reputation. Each honest act is a small signal, footsteps along a jetty slowly crossing a garden of noise. Fakes must survive many honest epochs to gain weight, costing attackers months of real time, capital locked per identity, and exposure of any cheating that resets the multiplier. Mass accounts yield near-zero influence each, making the attack pointless.
